The phrase "gazing grain" (line 11) is literally ripe grain in fields, and "gazing" personifies it as watching. This suggests a living world that looks on passively as the speaker passes. Option 1 fits.

The other options don't fit the text. Option 0 has no support, because the speaker has put away her labor. Option 2 is wrong because the house comes later and is a grave. Option 3 contradicts the poem's calm tone and Death's slowness ("he knew no haste").
